lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Listen up, here's the situation. As you can see, our little boat is tiny, half-rotten, and leaks in several places. If it lists to one side, we'll capsize and sink. And yet, there are so many of you today, and every single one of you has brought a ton of luggage. If you board with all this stuff, I'm afraid you're going to regret it. Especially those of you who can't swim.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: So how do we manage a safe crossing?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: I'll tell you. They board naked. Leave all the extra junk on the beach. Even then, the ferry will barely hold you. Hermes, it's your job from now on. Don't let anyone on board unless they're stripped bare and have thrown away their furniture. Stand by the gangplank, inspect them, and force them to board naked.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good point. We'll do exactly that. Right. Who's first?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I am! Menippus. Look, Hermes, I've already tossed my wallet and my stick into the lake. I didn't even pack my cloak, thank god.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Come aboard, Menippus, you excellent man. Take the premium seat up high next to the helmsman, so you can keep an eye on everyone. Now, who's this pretty boy?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: That's Charmoleos of Megara, the heart-throb. A kiss from him went for two talents.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Strip off the good looks, then. And the lips, with the kisses included, and the thick hair, and the blush on your cheeks, and the whole skin. That's fine. Travelling light. On you go. And you, the grim-looking fellow with the purple robe and the diadem. Who are you?

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: Lampichus, tyrant of Gela.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: So, Lampichus, why have you brought so much luggage?

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: What? Was a tyrant supposed to arrive naked, Hermes?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: A tyrant, no. A corpse, yes. Take it off.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: [sighs] There. I've thrown away my wealth.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Throw away the arrogance too, Lampichus. And the pride. They'll sink the ferry if they fall in with you.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: At least let me keep the diadem and the robe.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Absolutely not. Leave them.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: Fine. What else? I've dropped everything, as you can see.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Drop the cruelty, the stupidity, the insolence, and the rage. Leave those too.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: There. Bare as a bone.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: On you go. And you, the fat one, with all the flesh. Who are you?

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Damasias the athlete.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Ah, yes. I recognize you. I've seen you plenty of times in the wrestling schools.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: You have, Hermes. So let me aboard. I'm naked.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You're not naked, my good man, not wrapped in all that meat. Strip it off. You'll sink the boat if you so much as put one foot in. And throw away those victory crowns, and the herald's proclamations.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: There. Truly naked now, as you can see. Same weight as the other dead men.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Much better to be weightless. On you go. And you, Craton, put down the wealth, and the softness, and the luxury. Don't bring your funeral garments, or your ancestors' titles. Leave behind your lineage, your glory, and those times the city read your name out loud, and the inscriptions on your statues. And don't mention that they built you a massive tomb—even talking about it weighs us down.

lines.speaker: Craton
lines.text: Not willingly, but I'll throw it away. What else can I do?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good lord. And you in the armor, what do you want? Why are you carrying this trophy?

lines.speaker: General
lines.text: Because I won, Hermes. I fought bravely, and the city honored me.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Leave the trophy above ground. It's peaceful in Hades; we don't need weapons. Now, who is this solemn fellow, going by his get-up? Strutting around, eyebrows raised, deep in thought, with the massive beard?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: A philosopher of sorts, Hermes. Actually, a fraud, entirely full of nonsense. Strip him too. You'll find a lot of ridiculous things hidden under that cloak.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Take off the uniform first. Then all this other stuff. Good god, look at the sheer amount of charlatanism he's carrying! And the ignorance, the contentiousness, the vanity, the unanswerable questions, the thorny arguments, the convoluted concepts. And so much wasted effort, quite a bit of nonsense, humbug, hair-splitting... by Zeus, he's got gold in here! And hedonism, shamelessness, rage, luxury, softness—you didn't fool me, even if you kept it very well hidden. Drop the lying, too, and the arrogance, and the idea that you're better than everyone else. If you boarded with all that, what fifty-oared galley could hold you?

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Very well, I relinquish them, since you order it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Make him drop that beard too, Hermes. It's heavy and bushy, as you can see. That's at least five minas of hair.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good point. Off with the beard.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: And who is going to cut it?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Menippus here will take a shipbuilder's axe and chop it off, using the gangplank as a chopping block.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No, Hermes, hand me a saw. It's funnier.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: The axe will do. Excellent. You look much more human now that you've got rid of that goat-stink.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Want me to shave a little off the eyebrows, too?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: By all means. He's raised them way over his forehead, straining upwards for god knows what reason. [pause] What's this? You're crying, you scumbag? Terrified of death? Get on the boat.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: He's still got one incredibly heavy thing tucked under his arm.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: What is it, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Flattery, Hermes. It was very useful to him in life.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Well then, Menippus, you throw away your freedom, your outspokenness, your carefree attitude, your nobility, and your laughter! You're the only one here who's laughing!

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Absolutely not. Keep them. They're very light, very easy to carry, and quite useful for the crossing. And you, the rhetorician. Drop the endless verbiage, the antitheses, the balanced clauses, the periods, the barbarisms, and all the other heavy baggage of your speeches.

lines.speaker: Rhetorician
lines.text: There. I'm leaving it.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Perfect. Right, untie the mooring lines! Let's pull up the gangplank, haul the anchor. Hoist the sail. Steer us true, ferryman. Have a good crossing.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: [The boat is underway. The passengers wail.] What are you groaning about, you fools? Especially you, the philosopher who just got deforested.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Because, Hermes, I thought the soul was immortal.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: He's lying. He's upset about something else.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Like what?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That he won't get to eat any more lavish dinners. That he can't sneak out at night, wrapping his head in his cloak so no one recognizes him, to do a tour of the cheap brothels. And that he can't spend his mornings tricking young men out of their money in exchange for 'wisdom'. That's what's bothering him.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Oh, and you aren't upset to be dead, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: How could I be? Nobody even invited me—I hurried here myself. But hang on, speaking of which. Don't you hear a shouting? Like people yelling up on earth?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Yes, Menippus, and from several different places. There's a crowd gathered in the assembly, all laughing their heads off at Lampichus's death. His wife is being cornered by the other women, and his toddlers are getting pelted with rocks by the other children. Meanwhile, in Sicyon, they're applauding Diophantus the rhetorician while he delivers this Craton's funeral oration. Oh, and yes, Damasias's mother is wailing, leading a choir of women in a dirge for Damasias. But no one is crying for you, Menippus. You're lying there in total peace. All by yourself.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Not at all! Any minute now you'll hear the dogs howling a pathetic lament for me, and the crows beating their wings, when they gather to bury me.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You're a true gentleman, Menippus. Well, we've arrived. The rest of you, head straight down that path to the courthouse. The ferryman and I are going back for another load.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Have a good trip, Hermes! Let's get moving, guys. What are you waiting for? You have to be judged, and word is the sentences are brutal. Wheels, rocks, vultures. Every detail of your lives is about to come out.
